intro: Intelligence analysts turn scattered information into clear judgments, skills used in fraud, security and business analysis. The closest of the 25 careers below is fraud examination, with an 88% skill match, and every option needs no more education than you already have.
why_it_works: Your work means collecting information from many sources, testing what is reliable and briefing people who must act on it. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 3.62 out of 5 for this job, and coordination and judgment at 3.12. Fraud, cybersecurity and business intelligence roles use the same analysis. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Information Security Analysts earn $129,180 and are an 84% match; security certifications help.
Business intelligence roles value your briefing skills and have a median of $120,230 for their broader group.
Learn a programming or query language; it is one of your most common skill gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former intelligence analysts do?
faq.a: The closest matches are fraud examiners and analysts (88%), digital forensics analysts (86%) and private detectives and investigators (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Information Security Analysts are 84% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $129,180, one of the best-paid close options.

faq.q: Which jobs for intelligence analysts pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Compliance Managers at $141,900, Loss Prevention Managers at $141,900 and Information Security Analysts at $129,180, according to BLS May 2025 data. The two manager figures are for broader BLS groups, and those roles usually expect leadership experience.

faq.q: Do intelligence analysts need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than intelligence analysts already have, including all of the top 10. Many roles in this group expect a professional certification, such as a security or fraud credential, more than a new degree.

faq.q: What skills should intelligence analysts learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, managing people, troubleshooting and programming. Instructing already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so technical tools and team leadership are the main steps toward security and analytics roles.
